sections.title: California Interior Valleys: approximate vegetable planting windows
sections.text: UC Master Gardener guidance defines Interior Valleys as Sacramento, San Joaquin and similar valleys. Approximate windows include garlic October–December; spinach September–January; lettuce August and November–March; okra May; sweet corn March–July and August. Broccoli transplants are listed for December–February and July. These are broad gardening guidelines based on regional averages, not a commercial planting guarantee. Dates refer to seed except crops explicitly marked as transplants. Local microclimate, variety and current weather require checking.

sections.title: California vegetables: seasons and frost precautions
sections.text: UC Master Gardener guidance describes cool-season crops as generally growing best at average temperatures of 55–75°F, and warm-season crops at 65–95°F. These broad groups do not establish crop-specific seedling frost survival. Temperature, soil moisture and day length affect growth and quality. Check local first and last frost dates and protect frost-sensitive plants when frost is expected. Regional planting dates are approximate and may require local adjustment.
